Reddit has significantly more users, more traffic in corresponding subs, multireddits (Voat's sets feature is not being actively developed), live threads, private subs, a full-fledged flair system (Voat requires a sub to use CSS to accomplish this), modmail, AutoModerator, collapsed comment threshold setting, a more complete API, working RSS feeds, user friend/follow system, user block system, more advanced/effective search settings, ?context=_ option for comments, etc.

Voat has native 'expandos' (including WebM), sub block feature, public moderation logs, natively implemented night mode toggle, administrator-featured sub on the front page, no sponsored content excluding the occasional ad in the sidebar, certain major subs owned by the administrators (@system), commenting/posting restrictions if your account age is less than ~6 months and you've been downvoted below a certain CCP threshold, account deletion that also wipes all of your content, timestamps on content deletion, and all of its code available on GitHub (Reddit's code has become increasingly closed-source).

Overall, Reddit is superior on a feature level, though Voat natively implements many features that Reddit users usually need Reddit Enhancement Suite to use. Reddit's niche communities are far more active and superior simply due to their Voat counterparts usually being dead, inactive, or nonexistent; the quality of the larger subverses is something left to individuals to judge.
